documents.title: Delay in the supply of ceramic tiles
documents.text:
To: Claire Donovan, Project Manager
From: Hugo Reyes, Purchasing
Subject: Bellmont Residences: tile delivery

Dear Claire,

I have just spoken to our tile supplier, Calcera, about the order for the Bellmont Residences. Unfortunately, the company's kiln broke down last week and production has been halted for ten days. As a result, the first delivery, which was due on 3 July, will now arrive on 17 July at the earliest. The supplier has apologized and offered a credit of 3 percent on the invoice as compensation.

I have explored two alternatives. The first is to buy comparable tiles from Marrow & Sons, a local distributor, which could supply the full quantity within five days but at a price about 12 percent higher; the color is slightly different, and the architect would have to approve it. The second is to reorganize the work so that the tilers begin with the lobby and the corridors, for which Calcera has enough stock in its warehouse to deliver a partial shipment of forty percent on 8 July. The bathrooms, which need the remaining tiles, would then be done later.

I lean toward the second option, because it avoids both the extra cost and a design change, though it would require a new work schedule and a meeting with the tilers. Could we discuss it on Monday?

Best regards,
Hugo

documents.title: Introduction of a quiet hour
documents.text:
To: All employees, Cardew Marketing
From: Yvonne Baptiste, Managing Director
Subject: Quiet hour pilot, starting 6 October

After a number of staff suggestions and the results of our recent workplace survey, which showed that interruptions were the most frequent obstacle to concentrated work, we will begin a six-week trial of a daily quiet hour. Between 10:00 and 11:00 a.m. each weekday, meetings should not be scheduled, internal chat will be set to "do not disturb," and employees are asked to avoid approaching colleagues at their desks unless the matter is urgent. Telephone calls from clients will continue to be answered by the reception team, which will pass on messages.

The rule does not apply to the creative studio, where collaborative work often takes place in the morning, nor to employees on the client support desk. Staff who work in these teams may adopt a different hour by agreement with their managers.

At the end of the trial, we will ask everyone to complete a short questionnaire, and the leadership team will decide whether to continue, adjust or abandon the arrangement. I recognize that some of you may find the hour restrictive, and I welcome your comments in the meantime. A suggestion box has been placed in the kitchen, and you may also write to me directly.

questions.prompt: Why was the quiet hour introduced?
choices: Clients complained about noise in the building
Staff said that interruptions hindered their focus
Managers wanted fewer meetings in total
The creative studio asked for more privacy
questions.explanation: The survey showed that interruptions were the most frequent obstacle to concentrated work.

questions.prompt: What is NOT affected by the quiet hour?
choices: The scheduling of meetings during that hour
The working hours of the client support desk
Instant messaging between colleagues in the office
Visits to colleagues' desks unless urgent
questions.explanation: The memo restricts meetings, chat and desk visits; support desk staff may adopt another hour.

questions.prompt: What will happen after six weeks?
choices: The quiet hour will become permanent for everyone
The trial will be extended to cover the weekends
Employees will vote for a new managing director
The leadership team will decide what happens next
questions.explanation: Leadership will decide whether to continue, adjust or abandon the arrangement after the questionnaire.

choices: Its work gains from discussion between colleagues
Its staff were unhappy with the survey results
It never takes telephone calls from clients
It is managed directly by the managing director
questions.explanation: The memo says collaborative work often takes place there in the morning.

documents.title: Review: Lantern Bistro
documents.text:
Rating: 3 out of 5 · Visited on a Thursday evening with three colleagues

Lantern Bistro has been praised in local media for its seasonal menu, and the restaurant does not disappoint when it comes to ingredients. My duck breast was perfectly cooked, and the roasted vegetables that came with it tasted as though they had been picked that morning. A colleague's mushroom risotto was equally good, rich but not heavy. The wine list, though short, was thoughtfully chosen, and the waiter was able to suggest a bottle from a nearby vineyard that matched our dishes.

The problems began with timing. We waited forty minutes for the main course, during which nobody explained the delay or offered bread. When the food finally came, one dish was missing and had to be prepared again, so that we ate in two shifts. The manager apologized and took the missing dish off the bill, a courteous gesture, but it did not change the fact that our dinner had been spoiled. The dining room, though attractive, is also noisy; conversation across a table of four was difficult.

I would give the kitchen five stars and the service two. If the restaurant can solve its organization problem, it could be one of the best in the district. Until then, I would recommend it for a quiet dinner for two on a weeknight, and not for a group.

questions.prompt: What is the reviewer's main criticism?
choices: The food was too expensive for its quality level
The menu offers too few dishes for vegetarians
The restaurant is poorly organized during service
The wine list contains no products from the region
questions.explanation: Food was excellent but long waits and a missing dish show poor organization.

choices: A free bottle of wine was brought to the table
The delay was never apologized for at any point
The bill was lowered but the evening stayed spoiled

questions.explanation: The manager apologized and removed the dish from the bill, though dinner was already spoiled.

choices: polite

questions.explanation: The reviewer calls the manager's gesture a polite one.

questions.prompt: For which group would the reviewer recommend the bistro?
choices: Four colleagues attending a lively party
Tourists visiting at the weekend
Families with young children
Two people dining on a quiet weeknight
questions.explanation: The reviewer suggests it for a quiet dinner for two on a weeknight, not for a group.

documents.title: Pinecrest Storage: Self-storage units
documents.text: Need extra space? Pinecrest Storage offers clean, dry units in sizes from 1.5 to 20 square meters, available on a monthly basis with no long-term contract. Our small unit (3 square meters) costs 45 dollars per month, the medium (7 square meters) 90 dollars, and the large (15 square meters) 160 dollars. All units are protected by an alarm and cameras, and our site is open from 6 a.m. to 10 p.m. every day. The first month is half price for new customers who sign up online. Insurance is available for 8 dollars per month per 1,000 dollars of goods stored. We do not accept food, flammable materials or living things.

documents.title: Enquiry about storage
documents.text:
Hello,

I will be moving abroad for a year starting in September and want to store the contents of a one-bedroom apartment: a sofa, a bed, a desk, about fifteen boxes and a bicycle. I think the medium unit would be big enough, but I would like your opinion. I would also like to insure everything for about 4,000 dollars. Could you tell me how much I would pay for the first three months and whether I need to be present when the unit is opened or if a friend could collect items on my behalf?

Thank you,
Leonie Baptiste

documents.title: Re: Enquiry about storage
documents.text:
Dear Ms. Baptiste,

For the items you describe, the medium unit should be sufficient if you stack the boxes. Many of our customers in your situation find that 7 square meters is a comfortable fit for a one-bedroom apartment. Insurance for 4,000 dollars would cost 32 dollars per month. Your first month would be half price if you reserve online before the end of this week; after that, the standard price applies.

A friend may collect items provided that you give us a written authorization and a copy of your identity document, which we will keep on file. Because your stay is long, I would recommend paying quarterly; we offer a 5 percent reduction for payments made three months in advance.

Kind regards,
Nikhil Rao, Customer Advisor

choices: Finding a furnished apartment in a foreign city
Choosing suitable storage for her belongings

questions.explanation: She asks about unit size, insurance, cost and access.

documents.title: Request for time off
documents.text:
To: Sandra Whitlock, Head of Human Resources
From: Callum Reid, Accounts Department
Subject: Request for unpaid leave, 1 March to 25 April

Dear Sandra,

I am writing to request eight weeks of unpaid leave from 1 March to 25 April. My father is recovering from surgery and will need help at home during that time, and my sister, who would usually take care of him, will be abroad for work. I have already used my annual leave for this year and prefer not to leave my team short at year end, which is why I am proposing to begin after the accounts are closed.

I have discussed my work with my manager, Rina Takahashi, who is willing to redistribute my tasks. I would complete the VAT returns before I leave and will prepare detailed handover notes for my colleague, Ben Okoye, who has agreed to cover the month-end reports. I would remain available by e-mail for urgent questions, although I would not be able to work.

If the leave cannot be granted in full, I would consider working part-time over a longer period. Thank you for considering my request.

Best regards,
Callum

documents.title: Policy: Unpaid leave
documents.text: Employees with more than two years of service may request unpaid leave of up to eight weeks per calendar year for family reasons. Requests must be made at least six weeks in advance and approved by the manager and Human Resources. Leave exceeding four weeks requires a written plan for work coverage. Health insurance contributions by the company continue during the first four weeks only; after that, the employee must pay the premium. Seniority continues to accrue, but pension contributions are suspended during unpaid leave.

documents.title: Re: Request for time off
documents.text:
Dear Callum,

Thank you for the detailed message and for the plan you have prepared. I have checked the policy: you qualify with your three years of service, and your request uses exactly the eight weeks that the policy allows. I have approved it. Please note that after the first four weeks, you will need to pay your health insurance premium yourself, and I will send the details. I would also ask you to meet Ben before 15 February to complete the handover.

I hope your father makes a swift recovery.

Kind regards,
Sandra Whitlock
